transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

When a tumble dryer cuts out after about 10 minutes and then restarts once cooled down, it is almost always triggering its safety thermostat because it has overheated. This is most commonly caused by restricted airflow rather than a broken part. Please switch off and unplug the machine first. Then:
1. Check the main fluff filter (usually in the door opening) – is it full of lint or clean?
2. Inspect the vent hose going out the window – is it kinked, squashed, or blocked with fluff? Let me know what you find with these two checks.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
filter is clean, i do it every time. hose is squashed behind the dryer where i pushed it back, got fluff in the folds. also the cabinet gets really hot before it stops

That squashed hose with fluff in it is probably why your cabinet gets so hot. The dryer needs clear airflow to cool itself down; when the air path is blocked by the kink and lint, heat builds up inside until a safety thermostat trips and cuts the power. Once you unplug it, please straighten the vent hose completely, remove any fluff from inside it, and make sure the flap outside opens freely.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok will sort the hose. model on the label inside the door says IDV 75 if u need it

That squashed hose is most likely the main culprit for the heat buildup. Before you run it again, please check if your IDV 75 has a condenser unit or second filter (usually behind the bottom grille or inside the door). These collect fine lint that doesn't go in the main filter and can block airflow just as badly. If it's clogged, clean it thoroughly with water and let it dry fully before refitting. Once you've done this and fixed the hose, run a cycle to see if it stays on. If it still cuts out after 10 minutes despite clear airflow, the thermal cut-out itself may have failed and would need replacement by an engineer.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
not sure what a condenser is, mine vents out the window. ill sort the hose and run it again. is it ok to use it till then?

It is not safe to use it until you have fixed that squashed hose. The heat building up inside could damage the machine or create a fire risk if lint ignites.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.

candidates: Blocked airflow causing overheating and thermal cut-out (high)
Kinked or blocked vent hose restricting airflow (medium)
Failing thermal cut-out or thermostat (less likely if airflow is clear) (low)
